title: Fix double-escaped ampersands in Markdown image alt and title attributes
body: ## Changes - Fix double-escaped ampersands in Markdown image `alt` and `title` attributes, e.g. `![A & B](../assets/diagram.svg "C & D")` rendered `alt="A & B"`. ## Root cause Markdown images are round-tripped through a `__ASTRO_IMAGE_` markup attribute: `rehypeImages` JSON-serializes the image's properties (including `alt`/`title`) into that attribute, and the final `` is rendered later by decoding it again. The decode step only handled the quote character references the Markdown processors emit — remark writes `"`/`'`, satteri writes `"`/`'` — so an ampersand in the JSON survived the decode as entity text (`&` or `&`) and was escaped a second time when the attribute was finally rendered. The decode chains in `vite-plugin-markdown/images.ts` (3 sites — this code is inlined into the browser bundle, so it stays self-contained) and `content/runtime.ts` (1 site) now decode the ampersand references as well, in both styles, **ampersands last**: quotes are decoded first so that a literal `"` in the operator's own alt text is not mistaken for one the serializer wrote, and only then is `&` un-escaped. Literal entity text in the source is preserved. ## Testing - Extended the `core-image-remark-imgattr` fixture with `![A & B](../assets/penguin2.jpg "C & D")` and asserted via cheerio that the rendered `alt`/`title` are `A & B` / `C & D` (cheerio returns the decoded DOM value, so a double escape shows up as a literal `&`). - Verified the test bites: with the ampersand decoding removed the new test fails (`actual: 'A & B'`), with it restored it passes. - Ran the surrounding suites for regressions: `core-image*` (215 pass), `astro-markdown*` (47 pass), `units/content-collections/image-references` (11 pass), `units/content-layer/asset-imports` (3 pass). All green. - Changeset added: `.changeset/fix-image-attr-ampersand.md`. ## Docs No docs change needed — the documented behavior of image `alt`/`title` is unchanged; this restores it. --- Disclosure: implemented with AI assistance (Claude); the root-cause analysis, fix, and verification are mine and I can explain every line of the diff.
